prompt: First-person view from a Counter-Strike player holding an AK-47 at chest height, the weapon's wooden foregrip and iron sights centered in the frame. The gun's barrel points down a narrow dust-colored alleyway with crate stacks and a bombed-out doorway ahead. Bullet decals pepper the concrete wall to the left, and a flashbang grenade mid-arc trails a white smoke wisp at the upper right. The HUD shows 87 health, 24/90 ammo in a minimal sans-serif font at the bottom corners, and the lighting is the flat, slightly overlit quality of a Source engine map with baked shadow maps and low-res graffiti textures on the walls.

First-person perspective looking through the scope of an AWP sniper rifle in a Counter-Strike competitive match, the circular reticle framing a long sightline down a mid-lane between two concrete buildings. A single enemy player model is visible crossing the gap, motion-blurred at the crosshair. The scope's black vignette frames the zoomed view, and the unscoped periphery is a dark blur. The kill feed in the upper right shows recent eliminations in red and blue text, and the round timer reads 0:47 at the top center.

First-person VR perspective from the top of a Renaissance cathedral synchronization point in an Assassin's Creed-style world, looking down over a sprawling Italian city of terracotta rooftops, bell towers, and piazzas. The player's gloved hands grip the stone eagle gargoyle at the tower's peak, knuckles white, and the hood's fabric edge frames the top of the view. The city stretches to a hazy river and distant hills, and the golden-hour lighting casts long shadows across the tiled roofs. Eagle cry audio visualized as a subtle radial pulse at the screen center. Animus glitch artifacts—horizontal scan lines and blue digital fragments—flicker at the frame's edges.

First-person VR view of a hidden blade assassination in an Assassin's Creed-style game, the player's left forearm extended, the retractable blade emerging from a leather bracer toward a guard's back in a crowded marketplace. The blade's steel edge catches the warm Mediterranean sunlight, and the crowd of Renaissance-era NPCs in doublets and shawls parts slightly around the player. Market stalls with draped fabrics and hanging meats blur at the periphery, and a detection meter fills amber in the upper corner. The character models have high-poly faces with subsurface skin scattering and cloth physics on their garments.

First-person Minecraft view of a diamond pickaxe mid-swing striking a block of obsidian in an underground lava cavern. The pickaxe's pixelated blue head and wooden handle extend from the lower right, and cracks spider across the obsidian block's dark purple face. Lava flows in bright orange pixel columns two blocks away, casting a warm glow on the surrounding stone. The hotbar at the bottom shows torches, cobblestone, and a water bucket, and the health and hunger bars are full. The entire scene is rendered in Minecraft's signature 16x16 texel resolution with hard-edged shadows and no anti-aliasing.

First-person Minecraft view from the top of a player-built castle tower at sunset, looking out over a blocky landscape of forests, rivers, and distant mountains. The player's hand holds a map item, the pixelated parchment partially unrolled showing green and brown terrain squares. The sky is a gradient of orange and pink pixel bands, and square clouds drift at the horizon. Torches on the tower's crenellations cast a warm cube-shaped glow, and a creeper is barely visible at the tree line below. The debug coordinates read X: 847 Z: -312 in the upper left.

First-person cockpit view from a Formula 1 car at 280 km/h on a rain-soaked circuit, the steering wheel's carbon-fiber rim and LED shift lights filling the lower frame. Raindrops streak horizontally across the visor, and the track ahead is a grey ribbon of spray kicked up by the car in front. The halo device frames the top of the view, and the digital dash displays RPM, gear position, and lap delta in bright LCD segments. The side mirrors show blurred following cars, and the tire barrier and grandstands are motion-smeared at the track's edge. Photorealistic water simulation with puddle reflections and rooster-tail spray.

First-person view from inside a rally car cockpit on a dirt stage through a Finnish forest, the co-driver's pace notes visible on a clipped card to the right. The windshield is splattered with mud, wipers carving arcs through the brown film, and the gravel road bends sharply left through a wall of birch trees. The driver's gloved hands grip a suede-wrapped steering wheel, and the roll cage's tubular steel frame fills the cabin's upper edges. The speedometer needle bounces at 140, and the car's bonnet is dented and dusty. Realistic motion blur on the trees and soft-body suspension physics visible in the dashboard vibration.

First-person VR view from inside a Beat Saber session, two glowing energy sabers—one red, one blue—held in each hand at the ready. A corridor of neon-lit blocks approaches in rhythm, red blocks angled left, blue blocks angled right, with arrow indicators showing slice direction. The dark void background pulses with bass-reactive light bars in magenta and cyan, and a trail of sliced block halves tumbles away behind the incoming wave. The score counter reads 892,450 in the upper center, and a combo multiplier of x8 glows at the side. The visual style is clean, high-contrast neon geometry with bloom lighting and motion trails on the saber tips.

First-person VR view from Half-Life: Alyx, the player's left hand reaching for a glowing resin capsule on a shelf in a dilapidated City 17 apartment. The gravity gloves on both wrists glow faint orange at the knuckle plates, and the right hand holds a pistol at the hip, magazine half-visible. The apartment is trashed—peeling wallpaper, overturned furniture, Combine propaganda posters on the walls. A headcrab sits motionless on a table in the mid-ground, and the Combine health station on the wall hums with a red light. Volumetric light pours through a cracked window, illuminating dust. Source 2 rendering with high-fidelity PBR materials, finger-tracked hand models, and physically accurate glass refraction.

First-person VR view from Superhot, the player's right hand catching a red crystalline pistol mid-air in a stark white room. Time is nearly frozen—a red glass humanoid figure shatters in slow motion to the left, fragments suspended, and a bullet trail is visible as a faint red line inches from the player's head. The left hand is open, reaching for a bottle on a white table to throw. The entire scene is rendered in Superhot's signature minimal aesthetic—featureless white geometry, bright red enemies, black weapons, no textures, no HUD except the word SUPER HOT repeating faintly in the background.

First-person VR view from Skyrim, the player's left hand casting a fire spell, orange flames swirling from an open palm, while the right hand grips an iron sword. A frost troll charges through knee-deep snow in a mountain pass ahead, arms raised. The spell's glow lights the snow and the troll's white fur in warm tones, and the sword's edge catches the cold blue ambient light. Snowflakes drift across the view, and the HUD shows a health bar, magicka bar draining, and a compass with a quest marker at the top. The art style is Skyrim's characteristic painterly realism—detailed normal-mapped textures on the armor gauntlets, volumetric fog in the pass, and slightly stiff NPC animation on the troll.

First-person Minecraft view with RTX ray-tracing shaders enabled, the player's hand holding a torch inside a ravine. The torch casts realistic dynamic shadows and warm bounced light across the blocky stone walls, and lava at the bottom of the ravine emits a physically accurate orange glow with caustic reflections on the water stream beside it. The blocks retain their 16x16 pixel textures but now have parallax depth and specular highlights. The sky visible through the ravine's top is a deep starfield with a square moon. The hotbar shows an iron sword and a stack of 43 cobblestone.

First-person VR view from a Resident Evil-style survival horror game, the player's shaking hands holding a pump-action shotgun in a dim mansion hallway. The flashlight mounted on the barrel cuts a narrow cone through the darkness, illuminating peeling floral wallpaper and a overturned grandfather clock. Blood smears lead to a closed door at the end of the hall, and a shadow moves in the gap beneath it. The ammo counter in the lower right reads 3 shells, and the inventory shows a first-aid spray and a rusty key. The rendering is photorealistic with film-grain overlay, chromatic aberration at the edges, and a narrow depth of field that blurs the far doorknob.

First-person VR view from a Pavlov VR tactical match, the player's left hand pulling back the charging handle on an M4 carbine while the right hand steadies the magazine well. The bolt carrier is visible in the ejection port, and a spent brass casing is mid-flight to the right. The player stands in a concrete killhouse with plywood target silhouettes downrange, and another player in tactical gear crouches behind a barrier to the left. The lighting is flat overhead fluorescent, and the weapon model has detailed PBR textures—scratched anodized aluminum, worn Picatinny rails, and a dirty red-dot optic.

First-person VR view from No Man's Sky, the player's multi-tool scanner raised toward a massive alien flora specimen on a vivid purple-and-teal planet surface. The scanner's holographic readout projects species data and element composition in floating amber text beside the plant. The player's exosuit glove is visible gripping the tool, and the planet's horizon shows rolling hills of magenta grass under a sky with two visible moons and a ringed gas giant. The art style is No Man's Sky's signature procedural palette—saturated complementary colors, soft cel-shaded lighting, and slightly rounded low-poly terrain geometry.

First-person VR view from a Boneworks-style physics sandbox, the player's right hand gripping a crowbar mid-swing at a wooden crate in a brutalist concrete warehouse. The crate splinters at the impact point, wood fragments and physics-driven debris scattering outward. The left hand is open, reaching to catch a loose item tumbling from the crate. The warehouse has industrial pipe runs, flickering strip lights, and stacked barrels. The visual style is semi-realistic with baked GI lighting, and the player's arms show full IK-driven articulation with visible forearm twist matching the VR controller rotation.

First-person view in a retro PS1-era low-poly horror game, the player's blocky hand holding a pixelated flashlight in a foggy school corridor. The walls are flat-shaded polygons with warping low-resolution textures, and the flashlight beam is a hard-edged cone of yellow with no falloff. A humanoid figure with visible polygon seams and a jittery idle animation stands at the far end of the hall. The floor has affine texture warping typical of PS1 hardware, and the draw distance is severely limited, the corridor disappearing into solid black fog after twenty feet. No HUD, just a VHS-style tracking line wobbling across the bottom.

First-person VR view from Gorilla Tag, two oversized gorilla hands in the foreground, the left planted on a tree branch, the right reaching for the next in a forest canopy. The hands are bright orange with simple flat-shaded geometry and no fingers—just rounded stumps. The forest is a low-poly playground of chunky green trees, smooth boulders, and a rope bridge. Other gorilla players in neon colors swing through the branches in the background. The sky is a simple blue gradient, and the art style is aggressively minimal—no textures, just solid vertex colors, soft ambient occlusion, and a bright, cheerful palette.

First-person cockpit view from a Gran Turismo-style sim racer, looking through the windshield of a Porsche 911 GT3 at the Nürburgring Nordschleife on a dry afternoon. The Alcantara steering wheel fills the lower frame, stitching and center stripe visible, and the hands grip at ten and two in racing gloves. The dashboard's analog tachometer redlines at 9,000 RPM, and the track ahead rolls through the Karussell's banked concrete. The Armco barriers and spectator fencing blur at the track edge, and the Eifel forest is a wall of green behind. The rendering is photorealistic—accurate car-paint metallic flake, real-time reflections in the side glass, and tyre rubber marbles visible on the racing line.
